rationale: The buyers here are individual developers and sysadmins — a segment that overwhelmingly expects CLI tools to be free and open-source; there is essentially zero willingness-to-pay signal for a TUI network monitor. Operational autonomy is very low because the product is a downloadable tool, not a service Claude can deliver and bill automatically. Even if built and polished, monetisation requires a large free-user funnel that a solo non-technical operator cannot realistically sustain.
solution_plan: Not recommended for build. This is a developer utility that lives and dies by GitHub stars and open-source adoption. A solo non-technical operator using a Claude factory cannot realistically build a native TUI application (it requires systems-level Rust/C code, OS-level socket APIs, testing on multiple Linux distros) nor monetise it — the market expects this kind of tool to be free. Attempting to sell it as a paid SaaS or paid download would face immediate rejection from the target segment.
